title: acs v1: single-binary persistent ssh sessions
description:
Implement `acs` as designed in `docs/DESIGN.md`: one Rust binary that is the
local client, the per-connection remote proxy and the per-session remote
master, replacing the `dsh` shell function (ssh + dtach).

Invariants every child must preserve:

- Unfiltered stream: pty bytes reach the local terminal verbatim; keystrokes
  reach the pty verbatim except the command key (DESIGN §2, §6).
- Transport is the system `ssh`; no ssh-side configuration (DESIGN §3).
- Lossless resume after a network drop (DESIGN §5.2).

Done when every child is closed and DESIGN.md's Status reads Built.

title: Scaffold the acs crate: size-tuned profile, role dispatch, verify script
description:
Create the Cargo project the rest of the plan builds on (DESIGN §9).

- `Cargo.toml`: release profile `opt-level = "z"`, `lto = true`,
  `codegen-units = 1`, `panic = "abort"`, `strip = true`. Dependencies kept
  minimal: `rustix` (or `nix`) and `lexopt`; no async runtime, no clap.
- `src/main.rs`: role dispatch — default client; hidden `_proxy`, `_master`,
  `_install`, `_version`. Stubs are fine.
- Module skeleton per DESIGN §9 layout (`proto.rs`, `client/`, `master/`,
  `proxy.rs`, `install.rs`) and an `xtask/` workspace member placeholder.
- `scripts/verify.sh`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`,
  `cargo test`, `npx markdownlint-cli2` on `**/*.md`.
- Flip DESIGN.md `Status:` to "In progress" and its CLAUDE.md index row, in
  the same change (repo convention).

Acceptance: `scripts/verify.sh` passes; `cargo zigbuild --release --target
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` build; the slim
binary size for each target is recorded in the PR/commit message as the
baseline against the < 1 MB budget.
close_reason: Crate scaffold, size profile, role dispatch, verify script; slim release: x86_64-musl 320280 B, aarch64-musl 297928 B, aarch64-darwin 286080 B

title: Frame codec, message types and ACS-READY marker
description:
Implement the wire protocol of DESIGN §5.1 in `proto.rs`.

- Frame: `type u8 | len u32 BE | payload`. Hard maximum frame length
  (e.g. 1 MiB) rejected as a protocol error.
- Incremental decoder that accepts arbitrary read boundaries.
- All message types: HELLO (incl. client identity, `force`, TERM, COLORTERM,
  size, optional resume{instance, offset}), WELCOME (resumed/gap/fresh,
  created), BUSY, DATA (u64 offset), INPUT (u64 seq), ACK, RESIZE, PING/PONG,
  DETACH, KILL, EXIT, TAKEOVER, STATUS/STATUS_REPLY, ERROR.
- `PROTO_VERSION` constant; the `ACS-READY <proto>\n` marker and the
  `ACS-NEED <os> <arch>` line (DESIGN §3, §8): emit and a scanner that
  discards arbitrary preceding noise.

Tests: round-trip every message; decode with the input split at every byte
boundary; oversize and unknown-type frames error; marker found after
shell-rc noise and across split reads.
close_reason: proto.rs: frames, all message types, incremental decoder, ACS-READY/ACS-NEED scanner; 9 unit tests

title: Resume buffers: output ring with u64 offsets and input ack tracking
description:
Data structures behind lossless resume (DESIGN §4.2, §5.2).

- Output ring: append bytes, monotonically increasing u64 offsets,
  configurable capacity (default 1 MiB); `read_from(offset)` returns
  data / Gap (overwritten) / Future (invalid). Tracks the unsent watermark of
  the attached client so the master can apply backpressure.
- Input tracking: client-side queue of sent-but-unacked bytes (push, ack up
  to seq, iterate for resend); master-side dedupe that writes only the part
  of a resent INPUT beyond the last written seq.

Tests: wrap-around; gap detection exactly at the boundary; resend that
partially overlaps what the master already wrote is not duplicated.
close_reason: resume.rs: OutputRing (u64 offsets, gap/future, backpressure room), Unacked (client resend/rebase), InputDedupe (master); WELCOME gains input_seq; 9 unit tests

title: Command-key detector: Ctrl-] Ctrl-] then d (detach) / x (exit)
description:
Pure state machine for command mode (DESIGN §6.1-6.3), fed stdin bytes plus
an injected clock; outputs bytes to forward, actions (Detach, Exit) and the
next deadline.

- First Ctrl-] held up to 400 ms; a lone Ctrl-] or Ctrl-] + other key is
  forwarded as typed. Ctrl-] Ctrl-] within the window enters command mode;
  `d` / `x` act; any other key, or 2 s of nothing, forwards all held bytes.
- Recognise all encodings: legacy `0x1D`; kitty `CSI 93;5u` including event
  types `:1/:2/:3`; modifyOtherKeys `CSI 27;5;93~`. Consume whole escape
  sequences (never match inside one); buffer sequences split across reads;
  release events follow their press (forwarded or swallowed together).
- Bracketed paste (`CSI 200~` ... `CSI 201~`) passes through untouched.
- Escape key and window configurable (`ACS_ESCAPE_TIMEOUT_MS`).

Tests: table-driven `(bytes, timings) -> (forwarded, action)` covering every
rule above, including a pasted `^]^]d` and a terminal reply (`ESC`-prefixed)
arriving while a Ctrl-] is held.
close_reason: keys.rs Detector: legacy/kitty/modifyOtherKeys, releases, split reads, bracketed paste, passive replies/mouse, timeouts, configurable key; 20 table tests

title: Terminal mode observer and reset-on-detach sequences
description:
Passive scanner over the output stream that records which terminal modes the
remote program has turned on, and produces the matching resets for detach,
exit, or an abandoned reconnect (DESIGN §6.4). It must never modify, delay or
reorder the stream.

Modes: mouse (1000/1002/1003/1006/1015), bracketed paste (2004), alternate
screen (47/1047/1049), cursor visibility (25), focus events (1004), kitty
keyboard stack (`CSI > flags u` / `CSI < u`), modifyOtherKeys (`CSI > 4;N m`).

Tests: each sequence split at every byte boundary; reset output matches the
recorded state and is empty when nothing was set.
close_reason: modes.rs ModeObserver: DEC modes (mouse, paste, alt screen, cursor, focus, DECCKM, 2026), kitty stack/set, modifyOtherKeys, keypad, scroll region; ordered reset; 7 tests incl. every split point

title: Session names and per-uid socket directory
description:
Everything about where sessions live (DESIGN §4.1, §4.4, §4.5).

- Name validation `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; default `main` or `$ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION`.
- Directory: `$ACS_SOCKET_DIR` or `/tmp/acs-<getuid()>` (never `$USER`,
  never `$TMPDIR`). Create `0700`; on existing path `lstat`: must be a real
  directory, not a symlink, owned by our uid, mode `0700` — else refuse with
  an error naming the owner and suggesting `ACS_SOCKET_DIR`.
- `sun_path` length check with a clear error.
- `flock` helpers for the per-session creation lock and the directory lock
  used by `--new` to pick the lowest free number.

Tests: symlinked dir refused; wrong mode refused; ownership check via an
injectable stat; too-long path; `--new` numbering with gaps and under
concurrent callers.
close_reason: session.rs: name rules, ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION, /tmp/acs-<uid> or ACS_SOCKET_DIR with symlink/not-dir/foreign-owner refusal and mode tightening, sun_path check, create/dir flocks, lowest free number; sys.rs libc wrappers; 13 tests

title: ssh command builder, option passthrough and remote prelude
description:
Build every ssh invocation (DESIGN §3, §7.1, §8).

- Session calls: transport options first (`-T -e none -o ControlMaster=no
  -o ControlPath=none -o ServerAliveInterval=0`), then the user's `-i`, `-p`,
  `-J`, `-F`, `-o` in the order given, then `[user@]host`, then the remote
  command. Side calls (`--list`, install) omit the transport options so they
  keep the user's multiplexing.
- ssh binary from `--ssh` / `ACS_SSH`, default `ssh` on PATH.
- Hidden `--transport-cmd <cmd>` that replaces ssh with a local command, for
  the integration harness (DESIGN §9.1).
- Remote prelude (POSIX sh) with the client version baked in: try
  `~/.local/share/acs/<v>/acs` then `/usr/local/lib/acs/<v>/acs`, `exec
  _proxy <session> <mode>`, else print `ACS-NEED $(uname -s) $(uname -m)`.
  Everything interpolated is shell-quoted (`-- command...` args are
  arbitrary).

Tests: argv snapshots for session vs side calls; precedence (a user
`-o ControlMaster=auto` comes after ours); quoting of hostile command args.
close_reason: ssh.rs: Transport argv (transport opts first for session calls, side calls keep multiplexing, user -i/-p/-J/-F/-o in order, -- before destination, ACS_SSH, --transport-cmd hook), sh_quote, versioned prelude run under sh -c; WELCOME carries session name; 7 tests incl. executing the prelude

title: Command-line parsing (dsh-compatible)
description:
`acs [ssh options] [user@]<host> [session] [-l|--list] [--new]
[--no-reconnect] [--force] [-v] [-- command...]` with `lexopt` (DESIGN §4.4,
§7, §7.1).

- `-r` accepted and ignored (reconnect is the default); `-l` is `--list`;
  ssh's `-l <login>` rejected with a hint to use `user@host` or
  `-o User=`.
- Invalid combinations rejected: `--list` with a session or `--new`;
  `--new` with a session name.
- `ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION` resolves the default session name.

Tests: table of argv -> parsed config / error message, including every
`dsh` invocation form.
close_reason: cli.rs: dsh-compatible parsing with lexopt; ssh -i/-p/-J/-F/-o passthrough in order; -r ignored; -l = --list with user@host hint; --new/--force/-v/--no-reconnect/--ssh/--transport-cmd; -- command; ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION; 8 tests

title: Master: daemon lifecycle, pty, child and peer-uid check
description:
`acs _master` process lifecycle (DESIGN §4.2, §4.5).

- Started by the proxy: double-fork, `setsid`, stdio to `/dev/null`; take the
  session creation lock; bind the socket **before** spawning the child;
  report readiness over a pipe (dtach's statusfd) so the proxy never races
  the bind.
- Child: `$SHELL -l` in `$HOME`, or the `-- command...` given; env `TERM`,
  `COLORTERM` from HELLO, `ACS_SESSION=<name>`.
- Reap the child on SIGCHLD, keep its wait status; unlink the socket on exit.
- Every minute re-check the socket path and re-bind if it was removed
  (tmpfiles cleanup).
- On every accepted connection verify the peer uid (`SO_PEERCRED` on Linux,
  `getpeereid` on macOS) and drop foreign uids.
- Instance id: random u64 minted at creation.

Tests: start a master in a temp `ACS_SOCKET_DIR` running `/bin/sh -c`; two
concurrent starts produce one master; child exit status observed; socket
removed on exit and re-bound after deletion.
close_reason: master.rs: spawn() with readiness pipe on fd 3, fork+setsid daemon, creation lock around check+bind, child on pty with setsid/TIOCSCTTY and TERM/COLORTERM/ACS_SESSION, SIGCHLD reaping, socket unlink on exit and re-bind after deletion, peer-uid check; tests: exit status, concurrent starts, rebind, missing session, protocol mismatch

title: Master: session protocol, takeover, resume, resize, kill
description:
The master's side of the protocol (DESIGN §4.2, §5.2, §5.3).

- HELLO handling with attach / create / attach-or-create; WELCOME with
  instance id and resumed / gap / fresh.
- One active client: a new attach sends TAKEOVER to the previous one.
- Output: pty reads go into the ring; DATA frames from the client's offset;
  backpressure while attached (stop reading the pty when unsent bytes would
  be overwritten); ring wraps freely while detached.
- Input: INPUT dedupe by seq, ACK.
- RESIZE via `TIOCSWINSZ`; on a fresh attach force a redraw by signalling
  `tcgetpgrp(pty)` with SIGWINCH even when the size is unchanged.
- PING/PONG; DETACH; KILL = SIGHUP to the child's process group, SIGKILL
  after 3 s; EXIT{status} to the client on child exit.

Tests (framed test client over the unix socket): resume from an offset
yields exactly the missed bytes; offset beyond the ring yields gap; a new
instance yields fresh; takeover; KILL kills a process group that ignores
SIGHUP; backpressure engages with a stalled client and not when detached.
close_reason: Master protocol verified by 10 integration tests: exact resume replay, gap and fresh attach, same-identity silent takeover vs BUSY + force, KILL SIGHUP then SIGKILL after 3s, backpressure for a stalled client and none while detached, resize, forced redraw on fresh attach, input dedupe

title: Proxy: connect-or-spawn master and relay frames
description:
`acs _proxy <session> <mode> --proto N` (DESIGN §3, §4.3).

- Resolve the socket directory; connect; on ENOENT/ECONNREFUSED unlink a
  stale socket and start the master (create modes only), waiting for its
  readiness report.
- Write `ACS-READY <proto>` to stdout before the first frame.
- Check the protocol version in the client's HELLO; on mismatch answer
  ERROR telling the user to finish or kill the session.
- Splice stdin/stdout <-> socket until either side closes.

Tests: stale socket replaced; two proxies racing to create converge on one
master; mismatched protocol version yields ERROR.
close_reason: proxy.rs: connect-or-start (retries when another master wins), ACS-READY, HELLO proto check, --new naming under dir lock, splice relay, --list; 7 integration tests via stdio incl. stale socket, racing proxies, mismatch, missing session, --new numbering, dropped client detaches

title: Session listing (--list) via STATUS
description:
`acs <host> --list` (DESIGN §4.3, §4.5).

- Master answers STATUS with name, attached/detached, attached identity (or
  last attached), creator identity, created-at, idle time, child command,
  size, acs version.
- `acs _proxy --list` enumerates `<dir>/*.sock`, queries each, reports and
  removes stale sockets; no `ps` parsing.
- Client prints an aligned table; `no sessions` when empty.

Tests: listing with attached, detached and stale sessions; output format.
close_reason: list.rs: side call to _proxy --list, STATUS_REPLY frames rendered as NAME/STATE/WHO/IDLE/AGE/COMMAND table, 'no sessions', not-installed case; tests: unit table + integration with attached, detached and stale socket

title: Client terminal: raw mode, guaranteed restore, signals
description:
Local tty handling (DESIGN §7).

- Raw mode with dtach's termios flags; the original termios restored on
  every exit path: normal return, SIGHUP/SIGTERM/SIGINT, and panic (drop
  guard plus signal handler, `panic = "abort"`).
- Self-pipe for signals; SIGWINCH surfaced as a resize event.
- Single-threaded `poll` loop skeleton with timers (escape timeout, pings).

Tests: termios flag computation as a unit test; a pty-based test that the
terminal is restored after the client is killed by a signal and after a
panic.
close_reason: tty.rs RawMode (dtach flags, suspend/resume) + emergency restore via panic hook and SIGTERM/HUP/QUIT/INT handlers; sys.rs termios/pty/poll/pipe/signal self-pipe/peer_uid/wait wrappers; pty-based tests prove restore after SIGTERM and after panic

title: Integration test harness: local transport, pty runner, producers
description:
Shared test infrastructure for everything end-to-end (DESIGN §9.1).

- Temp `ACS_SOCKET_DIR` and temp `HOME` per test.
- Run the client under a pty with `--transport-cmd` pointing at the built
  binary's `_proxy` (no ssh).
- Deterministic producers (numbered lines, binary patterns incl. escape
  sequences) and a byte-exact capture of the client's stdout.
- A framed test client for driving the master/proxy directly.
- Transport killer to simulate a network drop mid-stream.

Acceptance: a smoke test attaches, runs a producer, and asserts byte
equality of output; harness usable from `cargo test`.
close_reason: tests/common: Remote fixture (temp HOME with versioned install, socket dir, pid-recording transport wrapper to cut links), pty Client runner (keys, resize, wait_for, exit code), binary pattern producer; smoke tests prove prelude->proxy->master->pty chain byte-exact and ACS-NEED

title: Client: ssh transport, handshake and byte-exact session
description:
The client's session path without reconnect (DESIGN §3, §4.4, §5, §6, §7).

- Spawn ssh via the builder; sync on `ACS-READY` (discard noise, show it
  under `-v`); detect `ACS-NEED` and hand off to install.
- HELLO with TERM, COLORTERM, size; DATA written verbatim to stdout while
  tracking the last offset; stdin through the command-key detector into
  INPUT with seq; RESIZE on SIGWINCH.
- `d`: DETACH, restore terminal (with observer resets), print
  `acs: detached from <host>/<name> - reattach with: acs <host> <name>`,
  exit 0. `x`: KILL, wait for EXIT, exit with the child's status.
- On creating a session print `acs: new session '<name>' on <host>` on
  stderr before raw mode.
- Exit codes per DESIGN §7.

Tests (harness): attach-or-create, byte-exact output incl. escape sequences,
detach and re-attach, `x` ends the remote session, EXIT status propagated,
new-session message.
close_reason: client.rs: dial with marker sync, HELLO/WELCOME, raw mode, verbatim DATA with offset tracking, detector->INPUT with seq, RESIZE, d/x, new-session and reattach messages, mode resets, exit codes; 11 pty tests incl. 300 KB byte-exact output, detach/reattach, x, exit status, single-escape passthrough

title: Client: liveness, automatic reconnect and lossless resume
description:
Resume after network drops (DESIGN §5.2-5.4).

- PING after 3 s of silence; link dead after 10 s without a frame: kill ssh
  and redial with backoff 1 s -> 30 s, reset after a connection that lasted
  30 s. `--no-reconnect` disables.
- HELLO with resume{instance, offset}; handle resumed / gap (clear + redraw)
  / fresh ("session was restarted").
- Resend unacked input; drop keys typed while the link is known down, but
  keep command mode working (`d` detaches while down; `x` reports it needs
  the link).
- Status while disconnected: nothing for < 10 s; then one bottom-row line
  with save/restore cursor and the xterm title stack; one forced redraw
  after a resume that followed a status line.
- Cooked mode while ssh authenticates on redial (password / key touch).
- TAKEOVER ends the client with a message and the reattach hint.

Tests (harness): kill the transport mid-stream and assert the client's
stdout equals the producer's output byte for byte; input sent before the
drop is not duplicated; ring overflow while disconnected yields gap
handling; `--no-reconnect` exits on drop.
close_reason: reconnect.rs: Liveness (PING after 3s, dead after 10s), Backoff 1s->30s with reset, redial with resume, unacked resend, keys dropped while down but d works and x explains, status line + title stack, redraw via resize pair; 7 pty tests (cut, freeze, input once, --no-reconnect, detach while down, x needs link, gap) + unit tests; daemons close inherited fds

title: Client: immediate redial on network change
description:
Stretch goal from DESIGN §5.3: skip the backoff wait when the default route
changes (Wi-Fi switch, wake from sleep) — route socket / SCNetworkReachability
on macOS, netlink on Linux — where it is cheap to observe.

Tests: the reconnect scheduler redials immediately on an injected
"network changed" event.
close_reason: netwatch.rs: PF_ROUTE (address/interface messages only, ARP churn ignored) on macOS, NETLINK_ROUTE link/addr groups on Linux, FIFO injection for tests; offline wait redials at once on a change (max once per 2s) and resets backoff; unit tests + integration test (20s backoff bypassed)

title: Shared accounts: client identity and confirmed takeover
description:
Accident protection when several people use one remote account (DESIGN §4.5).

- Client identity `<local user>@<local hostname>`, overridable with
  `ACS_IDENTITY`, sent in HELLO; the master records attached and creator
  identities.
- Cross-identity attach gets BUSY{identity, since}; the client asks
  `take over? [y/N]` on the terminal, retries HELLO with `force` on yes;
  without a terminal it fails; `--force` skips the question.
- Same identity takes over silently (own dropped connection, own second
  terminal).

Tests (harness): same identity silent; different identity BUSY; force
takes over; non-tty without `--force` fails.
close_reason: Client identity (ACS_IDENTITY or user@host) in HELLO; BUSY answered with a cooked-mode [y/N] prompt naming who and since when, --force skips, non-tty declines; same identity silent takeover; ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION; 5 pty tests

title: Multi-user integration tests in a Linux container
description:
Prove isolation between Unix accounts (DESIGN §4.5, §9.1) in a Linux
container with two users (docker/podman; the macOS host cannot switch uids
without root).

- Another user's pre-created `/tmp/acs-<uid>` (squatted, and symlinked) is
  refused.
- A connection from another uid to a master's socket is dropped.
- Two users' `main` sessions are independent.
- The whole `cargo test` suite also runs on Linux musl in the container.

Acceptance: one script (`scripts/test_linux.sh`) runs it end to end.

title: Payload set: format, ELF trailer and Mach-O embed
description:
Carry slim remote binaries inside a complete binary (DESIGN §8.1).

- Payload set format: index of (target triple, compressed size, SHA-256,
  gzip bytes).
- ELF: trailer `[slim][P entries][index][magic + index offset]`, read back
  through `current_exe()`; writer used by xtask and by `_install --finish`.
- Mach-O: `embed-payloads` cargo feature using `include_bytes!` of a path
  supplied at build time.
- API: `own_target()`, `is_complete()`, `payload_for(target)`.

Tests: build a synthetic trailer and read it back; truncated or corrupt
trailer means slim, never a crash.
close_reason: payload.rs: blob format (gz entries + index + footer), build/parse, ELF trailer via current_exe, embed-payloads feature via include_bytes (build.rs ACS_PAYLOADS_FILE), own target (build.rs ACS_TARGET), uname->target map; dependency-free sha256.rs with FIPS vectors; corrupt/truncated input never panics

title: Remote self-install: ACS-NEED, versioned install, _install --finish
description:
Install `acs` on a remote on first contact (DESIGN §8, §8.1, §4.5).

- On `ACS-NEED <os> <arch>` map to a target. Case 1 (own ELF target):
  stream own file with `cat`. Case 2 (Linux target in P): stream gz(slim_r)
  to `gzip -dc > ~/.local/share/acs/<v>/acs.new.<token>`, then run
  `acs.new.<token> _install --finish --sha256 <digest>` with P on stdin,
  which appends the trailer, verifies the digest, renames to `acs`, and
  repoints `~/.local/bin/acs` (temp symlink + rename). Case 3 (macOS other
  arch): clear manual-install message.
- Random token per install so concurrent installs converge; missing `gzip`
  gives a clear error; side calls keep the user's ssh multiplexing; redial
  after install.

Tests (harness, local "remote" with temp HOME): install from slim fails
cleanly with the `cargo xtask dist` hint; complete binary installs and the
installed copy is byte-identical to the dist output for that target;
concurrent same-version installs converge; two versions coexist and each
serves its own client.
close_reason: install.rs: plan (self-copy for own target; gzip'd slim + payload blob for other Linux targets; clear errors otherwise), side calls, _install --finish (sha256 check, new file since running exe is ETXTBSY, atomic rename, ~/.local/bin symlink swap), once per run; --version lists installable targets; 6 integration tests incl. payload path via fake uname, concurrent installs, corrupt upload; verified dist binaries in docker

title: Prune unused remote versions
description:
Housekeeping from DESIGN §8: `_proxy` touches its version directory on
start; version directories untouched for 30 days with no running master of
that version (per STATUS) are removed at the next proxy start.

Tests: old unused version pruned; old version with a live master kept;
current version never pruned.
close_reason: prune.rs: proxy touches its version dir; at most daily (.pruned marker) removes other version dirs untouched for 30 days unless a live master reports that version (STATUS); unit test with backdated mtimes + integration test via proxy start

title: cargo xtask dist: slim builds, payloads, complete binaries, size budget
description:
Release build pipeline (DESIGN §8.1, §9).

1. Slim builds for `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin` (cargo) and
   `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`
   (`cargo zigbuild`).
2. gzip -9 the Linux slim builds into the payload set.
3. Complete Linux binaries by appending the trailer; complete macOS binaries
   by rebuilding with `--features embed-payloads`, then ad-hoc `codesign`.
4. Output `dist/<target>/acs` plus a size report; fail if slim > 1 MB or
   complete > 2 MB.

Acceptance: `cargo xtask dist` on this Mac produces all four; `codesign -v`
passes on the macOS ones; replace the size estimates in DESIGN §8.1 with the
measured numbers.
close_reason: cargo xtask dist builds 4 targets (zigbuild musl, native macOS), payload blob, complete Linux (appended) and macOS (embedded, ad-hoc signed, codesign -v ok), size report with budget; measured slim 473-602 KB, complete 1.10-1.21 MB; linux binaries verified in docker alpine (aarch64 native, x86_64 emulated)

title: Manual verification matrix against real hosts
description:
Check the things automated tests cannot (DESIGN §9.1) and record results
in `docs/VERIFICATION.md`.

- TUIs: vim (tag jump, mouse), Claude Code, htop, less; OSC 52 copy; a
  kitty-keyboard-protocol TUI (command key still works); local scrollback.
- Drops: `pfctl` block, Wi-Fi switch, laptop sleep/wake; output lossless.
- Install: macOS client -> Linux x86_64 and aarch64 hosts; Linux client ->
  next hop.
- Shared account: two identities, confirmation prompt.
- `-i` key selection against a host that needs it (e.g. corello).

title: Docs and migration from dsh
description:
Finish the rollout (DESIGN §10).

- `README.md`: install, usage, command keys, environment variables.
- DESIGN.md `Status:` -> Built, and its CLAUDE.md index row, in the same
  change.
- Migration note: run `acs` alongside `dsh`; then replace the `dsh` function
  in `~/.zshrc` with `alias dsh=acs` and drop the dtach dependency (the
  dotfile change is the user's to make).
